transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time today. 

Um, I guess I came in because... well, it's probably not a huge deal, but I've been having this trouble where I just can't seem to settle down. It feels like I got a motor running inside me all day long. I try really hard to be good and stay put, I really do, but if I have to sit still in one place—like at church, or out in the waiting room just now, or even just sitting at home—I start feeling really trapped. I just end up having to get up or do something. 

I hope that's the right kind of thing to tell you? I just want to figure out how to be a bit better about it, if that makes sense.
Have you been like this since you were a child?

Yes, doctor, I guess I have. Um... I hope it's alright to tell you this, I don't want you to think I was a bad kid or anything. I really tried to behave, I promise. 

But... well, back when I was a boy in school, the teachers were always having to move my seat around. I just couldn't seem to stay put, no matter how hard I tried. I'd accidentally talk out of turn, or... or I'd get in trouble for jumping up out of my chair before the class was even done. I wasn't trying to be disrespectful to them, it just sort of happened before I could stop myself. 

Does... does that answer your question okay? I can try to explain it better if I didn't say it right.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things most days?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I worry a little bit, like normal people do, right? Just about regular stuff. But I wouldn't say I worry a lot or anything like that. I try to stay pretty positive, mostly. 

Is... is it bad if I don't worry a lot? I hope I'm not giving you the wrong answer. I just don't want to make a big deal out of nothing, you know? I'm mostly just having that trouble with the... the motor feeling I told you about. Does that sound okay?
Before you were 12 years old, were these restlessness and impulse-control problems already causing trouble in more than one setting, like at school and at home?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I told you about school, and how the teachers had to move me around... but at home, I don't think it was too bad. I tried really hard to be a good helper for my mom. 

Sometimes she'd tell me to go play outside because I was underfoot, or she'd say I was acting like a wild Indian, running around the house when she was trying to rest. But I wasn't trying to be bad, I just had a lot of energy, you know? Like any normal boy. I don't think it caused real *trouble* at home, just... maybe she got a little tired of me sometimes. 

Is that what you mean? I hope I'm explaining it right. I don't want you to think I was a terror at home or anything, I really did try to be good for her.
Do you also often have trouble paying close attention to details or making careless mistakes?

Um, no, not really. I mean... I might miss a little thing here or there, but everybody does that sometimes, right? I try really hard to pay attention when people are talking to me or if I'm trying to do a task. 

I don't think I make a bunch of careless mistakes. I always try to do my best. I just... I get a little squirmy, like we talked about, but my attention is usually okay, I think. 

Did I answer that right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. I promise I'm not trying to hide anything, I just don't really have that problem.
Do you often lose things you need, like keys, schoolwork, or your phone?

Um, no, sir... I don't really lose my things. I mean, I try to be real careful with what I have. Sometimes I might put my phone down and forget which room it's in for a second, but I wouldn't say I *lose* it. 

I always make sure to put my keys in the exact same spot by the door so I don't mess up and cause a fuss. I really try to stay on top of that kind of stuff, so I'm not a bother to anybody. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I don't have that problem... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers for whatever you need.
Do you often blurt out answers before a question has been finished?

Um, well... I guess maybe sometimes I do that a little bit. But I don't ever mean to be rude, I promise! I just... I get real eager, I guess. 

Like, if I'm talking to my cousin, or the lady at the food pantry, or even the pastor... sometimes I'll just jump in with an answer before they're even done talking. I just think I know what they're gonna say and I want to show I'm listening, you know? But then... well, sometimes I realize I answered the totally wrong thing, or I end up making them mad because I cut them off. 

I always feel real bad when I do it. I try so hard to bite my tongue because I'm really not trying to be disrespectful to anybody. Does that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope it doesn't make me sound awful. I really do try to be polite.
